steps.note: Compare the destination against what the SOURCE was recorded doing at M1. Reads: compare-runtime-parity.py per admitted entry point, against verification/source-oracles/<slug>.json. Writes: compare-scenario-parity.py per scenario the approved corpus requires -- it restores the declared initial state, proves the destination is in it, replays the complete recorded request (body and headers included) and reads back every declared effect. Then compose the receipt-bound summary (compose-parity-receipt.py), where an entry point covered by scenarios passes only when every REQUIRED one passed. Expected values come only from the M1 capture; never from the card body, never from what the destination happens to return. Nothing here captures the source: that happened at M1, and re-capturing now would record the source's answer to a question the destination has already been asked.
G-1..G-4 measured against the referent. Each evaluator writes its own verdict; a REFUSE here is a real outcome, not something to argue with.

The runner, fail-closed: snapshot the test reports before any rebuild, parse surefire, refuse a card body that pre-specifies a verdict, assert the tree is retrievable, run the pinned feeding gates so their receipts exist, then assert-pinned-gates-ran, assert-g4-claim-consistency and assert-no-fence-evasion. Feeding gates must run before the receipts are asserted or the floor refuses on an empty directory.

Author the verdict from the measured exit codes only, with an explicit failed_floors, and compose the coverage account (compose-coverage-account.py) from decisions.yaml and the parity receipt so every ADR-retired source is accounted for. A non-empty failed_floors makes the verdict REFUSE; a remaining coverage gap is legal but must be visible in coverage_account. Checkers never author the verdict and the card body never pre-specifies it.

Lint what was just written: the verdict against its schema, the floor receipts, the claim tokens, and the coverage account against decisions.yaml and the parity receipt (assert-coverage-account.py). This step can only agree or refuse; it cannot change the verdict or the account.
